item.text:
I continued the 1B review round and recovered the missing digital-code source plus two independent lines on cyber-policy implementation and one stronger line on state-of-siege effects.

What changed:
1. The digital-code claim is now supportable with a precise underlying source.
2. The cybersecurity chapter now has at least one independent implementation step after strategy adoption: the Council National de CyberDéfense was created and staffed in August 2023.
3. The state-of-siege record now has a stronger independent outcome source from UNJHRO/MONUSCO plus Amnesty’s effectiveness critique.
4. I also found a local-language MONUSCO/Journalists in Danger source showing that insecurity and state-of-siege conditions were still constraining press work in North Kivu.

Key recovered sources:
1. Digital code primary text: Refworld hosts the national legislative text, and Droit-Numérique / the budget ministry page both identify the 13 March 2023 ordinance-law and its scope.  
- Refworld: https://www.refworld.org/legal/natleginstr/natlegbod/2023/fr/150225?prevDestination=search&prevPath=%2Fsearch%3Forder%3Ddesc&result=result-150225-en&sm_country_name%5B%5D=Democratic+Republic+of+the+Congo+%28the%29&sort=score&ss_collection_name%5B%5D=Case+Law&ss_collection_name%5B%5D=Legal+Instruments  
- Budget ministry page with the presidential promulgation and policy rationale: https://budget.gouv.cd/dantic/index.php/2017/02/23/the-worlds-largest-salt-flat-salar-de-uyuni-photographers-destination/  
- The budget page lines 39-47 state the law was promulgated by Tshisekedi and created the institutional framework for digital regulation, data protection, electronic proof, and related bodies.

2. Cybersecurity strategy and implementation:
- Presidency source on the 2022-2025 strategy: https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/la_strategie_nationale_de_cybersecurite  
- Relevant lines: 55-69 show it was validated by Tshisekedi, presented in Council of Ministers, and organized around seven axes including critical infrastructure, data protection, legislation, risk/crisis management, and cooperation.
- Actualite.cd on the ANCE decree: https://actualite.cd/index.php/2023/07/23/rdc-adoption-du-projet-de-decret-portant-creation-organisation-et-fonctionnement-de  
- Relevant lines: 107-113 show the government adopted the decree creating the Autorité Nationale de Certification Electronique and described its role in trust services and operationalizing the digital framework.
- UNE.CD on the CNC: https://www.une.cd/rdc-jean-claude-bukasa-nomme-coordonnateur-du-conseil-national-de-cyberdefense-par-ordonnance-presidentielle  
- Relevant lines: 212-223 show Tshisekedi named Jean-Claude Bukasa to head the Council National de Cyberdéfense, presented as an autonomous service under the presidency.

3. State-of-siege effects and independent implementation context:
- UNJHRO/MONUSCO year-end 2023 trends: https://monusco.unmissions.org/en/actualites/principales-tendances-des-violations-des-droits-de-lhomme-en-rdc-1er-janvier-au  
- Search result summary says UNJHRO documented 5,273 violations in 2023, a 12% decrease overall, but 4,473 violations in the five conflict provinces.
- The State Department report remains the strongest overall implementation cross-check: https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2107668.html  
- Relevant lines 8, 68, 82, 110, 138 show that the state-of-siege provinces had sharp civic-space restrictions, abuse under cover of the state of siege, and interference with assembly and expression.
- Amnesty’s 2023 critique is still the sharpest effectiveness judgment: https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/05/drc-authorities-must-end-state-of-siege/  
- It states the measure was repeatedly extended, fell far short of constitutional and international standards, and had not improved security.

4. Press and civic-space constraints in the east:
- MONUSCO / local-language report on journalists in Goma: https://peacekeeping.un.org/fr/goma-face-%C3%A0-l%E2%80%99ins%C3%A9curit%C3%A9-l…  
- Search result summary says JED counted at least 11 attacks or incidents against journalists in Nord-Kivu since the start of 2023, during the period of state of siege.
- CPJ coverage gives independent corroboration of the broader pressure pattern:
  - https://cpj.org/2023/04/drc-authorities-detain-2-journalists-threaten-another-with-arrest/
  - https://cpj.org/2023/06/congolese-soldiers-arrest-beat-3-journalists-covering-land-dispute/
  - https://cpj.org/2023/09/cpj-condemns-charging-detention-of-drc-journalist-stanis-bujakera/

Correction to the earlier ledger:
- `WEB-1B-05` should be retired or replaced. The current `budget.gouv.cd` URL was clearly mismatched to the claim in the earlier register, but the actual text is still recoverable from the budget ministry page and Refworld. The claim should be rewritten to point at the ordinance-law text and the budget ministry promulgation note, not the unrelated page path.

What this means for the chapter:
- The chapter is still stronger on formal adoption than on proven effectiveness.
- There is now a usable chain from policy design to formal institution creation for cybersecurity: strategy, digital code, ANCE decree, CNC appointment.
- There is still no strong independent 2023 evidence that these cyber institutions measurably reduced risk or improved security.
- For the state of siege, the evidence now more clearly supports “formal control with weak results” than “successful stabilization.”
